limitations: The initial provider executes explicit Galaxy/Trigger sources and paths or opt-in bounded automatic discovery through a supplied SC2 GameContentResolver; it does not open or infer an installation itself.

Catalog-backed fixed-step simulation is available when a resolved catalog is injected. Optional replay assistance consumes normalized semantic commands, reports divergence, corrects from complete tracker frames, and reconstructs backward seeks from a deterministic baseline; concrete selected-content ability resolution, semantic Trigger dependency-closure selection, and asynchronous host-native bridging remain incomplete. Trigger XML is lowered directly to the engine subset, with failures returned as diagnostics.

Simulation snapshot/restore currently preserves engine state and the deterministic tick but not queued commands, pending semantic events, or the fractional fixed-step accumulator; hosts must snapshot only at a drained tick boundary.
Runtime diagnostics are structured, but the existing engine's trace covers isolated execution errors only until the engine/sim implementation migration is complete.
